title: introduce-rag-stepwise-debugger-and-inline-assertion-kit
author: Anika Rao
description: Adds a lightweight stepwise debugger and inline-assertion harness to the RAG quickstarts and SDK examples. Motivation: teams repeatedly asked for a deterministic, reproducible way to step through retrieval+agent decisions during authoring and CI (see ENG-9123). This PR introduces: 1) a docs walkthrough (docs/rag/stepwise-debugger.md) that explains the mental model and recommended invariants for RAG debugging; 2) two minimal example toolkits (Python + TypeScript) that wire the debugger into the SDKs and surface per-step traces, token-level latencies, and assertion hooks; 3) an inline-assertion DSL that lets authors codify expected retrieval hits and tool-call side effects for regression tests; 4) a local-playground recipe for the docs site that lets authors run stepwise sessions in the browser via the devcontainer. Key goals: make step-by-step traces first-class, enable small automated regression checks in CI, keep the examples compact and copy-paste friendly. Changes include small SDK helpers (non-breaking) and docs-only site config. Checklist: [x] Write stepwise debugger doc and mental model, [x] Add Python example and assertion harness, [x] Add TS example and browser playground wiring, [x] Add small SDK helpers and feature flags, [x] Add quick CI smoke test snippets. How to validate locally: follow docs/rag/stepwise-debugger.md -> run examples/python/README.md or examples/ts/README.md -> run the included smoke script (scripts/smoke-debugger.sh) which runs against the local devserver. Related: linear ENG-9123, demo notes in PR conversation. Migration notes: no breaking API changes; SDK helpers are behind a feature flag and can be imported opt-in. Links: docs preview: https://redwood.dev/docs/rag-debugger (preview), linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9123.
